rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Confusion: The proton is made of three quarks ($uud$), but its mass is $938\\\,\text{MeV}/c^2$ while the sum of quark masses is only $\\\sim 10\\\,\text{MeV}/c^2$. The missing mass (99%) comes from the strong-field interaction energy within the proton - mass is NOT just the sum of parts.  ·  Confusion: There are only TWO stable hadrons found in nature: protons and electrons. Free neutrons decay ($\tau_{1/2} \\\approx 14.6\\\,\text{min}$). Free quarks are never found - color confinement means they only exist inside composite particles.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Elementary particles:** Particles with no known internal structure or substructure. They are the fundamental constituents of matter and radiation under the Standard Model of particle physics. Elementary particles fall into two classes: fermions (matter) and bosons (force carriers).  ·  **Fermions (spin-$\frac{1}{2}$):** Obey the Pauli exclusion principle. They include quarks and leptons. Quarks combine to form hadrons (baryons, mesons); leptons do not participate in the strong interaction. There are three generations of each.  ·  **Bosons (integer spin):** Do NOT obey the exclusion principle; they can occupy the same quantum state (lasers, BEC). Force-carrying bosons: photon ($\\\gamma$, EM), gluon ($g$, strong), $W^\\\pm/Z^0$ (weak), and the Higgs boson ($H^0$, scalar, spin-0).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • Hubble law — expansion of the Universe  ·  Confusion: A neutrino has almost no mass, but NOT zero mass. Oscillation experiments show $\\\Delta m^2 \neq 0$, so neutrinos must have mass. The absolute mass is unknown but $< 2\\\,\text{eV}$ (normal hierarchy).  ·  Confusion: Antimatter is NOT just a sci-fi plot device. Positron emission tomography (PET) uses $e^+e^-$ annihilation ($\\\gamma$-pair detection). Antiprotons are stored in the AMS-02 detector on the ISS to study cosmic rays.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Confusion: Not all particles with the same quantum numbers can annihilate. An electron and proton (both fermions, opposite charge) can form positroniumium but cannot annihilate into pure photons - charge conservation forbids $e^- + p \rightarrow \\\gamma + \\\gamma$, so they form Hydrogen instead.  ·  Confusion: Top quark ($t$) and bottom quark ($b$) are also called truth ($t$) and beauty ($b$) in older literature. The IUPAP standard names (top/bottom) are now universally used. Charmonium ($c\bar{c}$) and bottomonium ($b\bar{b}$) are real quarkonium states.  ·  Confusion: Color charge is an abstract SU(3) gauge charge analogous to electric charge, but with THREE types (+red, +green, +blue) instead of two. It's called "color" because it produces a color-force law analogous to electromagnetism - not because quarks have visible color.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Confusion: The Standard Model explains 3 of 4 fundamental forces (EM, strong, weak) but NOT gravity. Neutrino masses require a BSM (Beyond Standard Model) extension (e.g., Majorana masses, seesaw mechanism).  ·  Carefully distinguish between similar-looking concepts in particle physics.  ·  Pay attention to the conditions under which formulas and theorems apply.
